Outputs

Outputs depend on the analysis mode.

Shared outputs

AnnData objects can retain major cell-type labels together with spatial and intensity data.

Supervised outputs

These can include:

  • primary and subtype annotations;

  • cell-count/proportion tables;

  • percentages relative to parent populations and all cells;

  • phenotype-definition tables;

  • hierarchy visualizations; and

  • spatial overview, highlight, or custom plots.

Unsupervised outputs

Cell-type proportion matrices

Sample-by-population tables summarizing major cell-type proportions.

Pie plots

Optional sample-level visual summaries of population composition.

Discovered phenotype tables

Protein-marker-pattern phenotypes observed within selected parent populations, together with within-parent cell counts and proportions.

Phenotype-proportion matrices

Sample-by-phenotype tables for each explored parent.

AnnData phenotype annotations

Discovered phenotype host names are stored in adata.obs and pattern definitions in adata.uns.

Two-group comparison

When two groups are configured, SpPrAn reports common and group-specific phenotypes and descriptive abundance summaries.

Statistical results

Common phenotype proportions can be compared with two-sided Mann–Whitney U and Welch t-tests. Benjamini–Hochberg FDR-adjusted p-values are exported.

Intensity outputs

For selected markers, SpPrAn exports per-phenotype Tukey box-plot summaries and outlier values.

Full-mode outputs

Full mode produces exploratory outputs and then adds hierarchy-oriented supervised outputs based on the discovered phenotype definitions.

Interpretation

Phenotype proportions are conditional on the parent population used for discovery. For example, a phenotype representing 20% of T cells does not necessarily represent 20% of all cells in the tumor.

Statistical results should be interpreted together with detection frequency, effect magnitude, biological sample size, multiple-testing adjustment, and study design.
